title: Choosing Inner Freedom:
headline: No narrator. Two people who lived it tell it: Eloise, who was looking at a life sentence, and Eddie, who was lost. Both found something at their first workshop, both came home, and Eloise walked back into Chowchilla to give it to someone else.
story: This version is told only by people FTC changed, in their own words, like your inspiration reel. Eloise carries the story and Eddie answers her. There is no voice-over.

It opens on the stakes in their voices: <q>I was looking at a life sentence by means of my third strike</q> and <q>I was lost. I was hurt. I was in pain.</q> Then your intro. Then the first workshop: Eloise went with a friend who was serving life, and Eddie found <q>unconditional love</q> on a Sunday afternoon. <q>Maybe I can. Maybe I can. It started there at Chowchilla.</q>

They come home: <q>I've never heard you talk like that before.</q> <q>Where before I've taken, now I'm giving.</q> The climax is Eloise walking back into Chowchilla as a volunteer and thanking Angela, the volunteer who stayed with her: <q>Your face and your heart has been with me all these years.</q> Eddie: <q>I have the freedom to choose. And I did.</q> Eloise lands the theme your narrative opened with, in her own words: people can push her buttons, <q>but my life doesn't have to be chaotic in my mind and in my heart.</q>
Eddie hands it to the viewer (<q>It changes your lives. It changed my life.</q>), then the ask, each part on its own slide: the $300,000 goal, the giving levels, Donate now.

decisions.t: Told by Eloise and Eddie, no narrator
decisions.b: You liked the buttons voice-over. We kept its idea and gave it to Eloise: <q>people can come at me with rudeness and anger… but my life doesn't have to be chaotic in my mind and in my heart.</q> If you want one narrator line back, say which row.
Eloise's story needs women on screen. The Female Participants and Volunteers folder is not shared with atdhe@happypeople.me. Please share it; the stand-in frames come from your own reel until then.

Her 2023 Zoom is small. If you have a better recording of her, or of another woman who finished the program and is home, send it. And is Eloise still an FTC Volunteer? Her title says so, from her 2023 interview.
Three 4K interviews from the Stockton workshop (DSC_6587, DSC_6588, DSC_6591) haven't been reviewed. If Eddie is in one, it replaces the Zoom.

The finished cut uses your approved footage, but the preview pictures on this page come from older FTC films. Is anyone in them former staff, or someone who signed a no-photo release? Tell us which frame and we will make sure they never appear.
Out of the video until we have the study (who ran it, years, how many women, how a return was counted).

One check on the giving levels from your sheet: the first three work out to $50 per incarcerated student per month, but $1,000 for 3 students for 6 months is about $56 a month and $2,500 for 8 students for 6 months is about $52. Keep them as written, or send the corrected lines?
